children: Rep.
Ted Lieu
(D-Calif.) challenged the idea of granting artificial intelligence (AI) legal personhood, arguing that doing so could create serious legal consequences for AI companies and their models.
Lieu Challenges AI Personhood
On Saturday, Lieu wrote on
X
, "Math calculations, no matter how complicated, can never achieve personhood."
He challenged those who disagree with his position, arguing that recognizing AI models as persons could raise questions about how companies develop and test them.
"Disagree? Then the logical consequences are that we should prosecute AI companies for enslaving and testing on AI ‘persons,’" Lieu wrote.
He also questioned whether AI models recognized as persons should face legal consequences for their actions.
"And any AI model ‘person’ that breaks the law should also get prosecuted," he added.
